Hey @AnmanIndustries, you know anything about livestock guardian dogs?

I was going to say things about X breed in Australia and how even then its not very good about Y predator and that you would be better of doing Z for A animal in B situation, you know, my usual detail.

But uh, against people? I can give you information on dogs, cats, foxes, snakes even eels (they will eat baby chickens if big enough), but I can only give general advice.

In Australia it is quite common and it has actually stuffed me up before. I was going to purchase my previous lot of pigs from a farmer, but right at the last moment he had most of his sheep stolen and he was super upset and just called off all trading. They even took his dog apparently. So I ended up having to pay more for my piggies from a last minute deal. The biggest issue in these circumstances here though is that we have thousands upon thousands of acres of land that our herd animals live on and in short, there is no real way to protect against theft in these cases.

On smaller properties dogs are your best bet against people. As long as the property has a fully enclosed fence line, mostly so the dogs cant get out and unwanted animals cant get in (like other dogs), any large dog that barks at people will generally work. We have hunting dogs too, a roo dog and a pig dog and when they are just sitting there at a fence they are an intimidating deterrent. Most people who will try to steal from you will usually case a joint out. So what you would need to do is make sure you find a dog that doesnt mind being with animals. In most cases, its just a matter of training. EG, our dogs will not attack any animal we introduce directly to them, so they mostly ignore the cat, the rabbits and the various birds we have at my home. Most dog breeds can get along with most larger or equal sized animals without issues.

If you are worried that the dogs will not hear someone coming over the fence, your best bet then is to have an electric fence that also runs a power off alarm. If someone or something touches the fence, it will make a noise and alert the dogs. If someone cuts the wire, it will alert you instead. Or set up the alarm someone outside to get the dogs riled up. This does mean a bit of fiddling around. Normally you connect an electric fence to one power input and when something touches the line and the ground it completes the circuit, making you the conductor. We normally run a line around an entire pen and add the input. IF you want to power off alarm you can not create a loop of wire, so there needs to be a tiny gap somewhere. At the end of the line you have a device that triggers when the power has been removed. Its not normally standard equipment on average systems.
